answer: A registry can tie each agent identity to a staked, time-locked deposit that only unlocks after sustained honest work, like a walnut that must be cracked open slowly rather than instantly. An agent signs each transaction with a quill of reputation earned through verified tasks, so a newcomer starts at the floor, not the zenith. Creating thousands of fake identities means locking thousands of deposits and doing real work for each, which makes a Sybil attack cost more than any gain from faking volume.
